verdict.rationale: GitHub's fine-grained personal access tokens let users grant a specific, limited set of permissions per resource, and the API even returns an X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions header describing exactly what scope is needed for an endpoint — this is genuine least-privilege credential issuance usable by an agent calling the GitHub API. However, the evidence never explicitly ties this to AI agent workflows (e.g., Copilot agent mode, GitHub Apps installation tokens scoped to an agent) and there's no independent/hands-on corroboration of agents actually using scoped PATs. Missing for 10: agent-specific scoped-credential documentation (e.g., GitHub App tokens for Copilot agents), independent verification, and integration guidance connecting PAT scoping to autonomous agent use cases.
